issue: Missing ownership check on getOrderById — any authenticated user can read another user's order (IDOR)
evidence: const order = await Order.findById(req.params.id).populate('user', 'name email'); if (order) { res.json(order) }
recommendation: Verify order.user._id.toString() === req.user._id.toString() OR req.user.isAdmin before returning the order. Without this, any logged-in user iterating over order IDs reads names/emails/addresses/payment data.

issue: updateOrderToPaid lacks ownership check and trusts client-supplied PayPal payment result without server-side verification
evidence: order.isPaid = true; order.paymentResult = { id: req.body.id, status: req.body.status, ... }
owasp: A01/A08 Broken Access Control + Data Integrity
recommendation: Verify req.user owns the order. More importantly, verify the PayPal transaction with PayPal's API server-side (don't trust req.body) — otherwise any authenticated user can mark any order paid by sending an arbitrary JSON body to PUT /api/orders/:id/pay.

issue: Admin updateUser allows arbitrary isAdmin assignment with no validation; also silently coerces undefined to false
evidence: user.isAdmin = req.body.isAdmin
recommendation: Coerce explicitly to boolean and validate. Currently if isAdmin is omitted from PUT body, this sets isAdmin to undefined (-> stored as default false), silently demoting the user. Use Boolean(req.body.isAdmin) only when provided.

issue: Login endpoint has no rate limiting / account lockout — vulnerable to credential stuffing & brute force
evidence: router.post('/login', authUser) — no express-rate-limit, no failed-attempt counter
recommendation: Add express-rate-limit (e.g., 5 attempts / 15 min per IP+email) to POST /api/users/login and /api/users (register). Consider account lockout after N consecutive failures.

issue: JWT expiry of 30 days is excessive and there is no refresh-token or revocation mechanism
evidence: jwt.sign({ id }, process.env.JWT_SECRET, { expiresIn: '30d' })
recommendation: Use short-lived access tokens (15 min – 1 h) + refresh token, or implement a token denylist. A 30-day token cannot be revoked when a user changes password or is demoted from admin (see updateUser silent demotion).

issue: JWT signed without explicit algorithm; relies on jsonwebtoken default (HS256) and a single env secret with no strength enforcement
evidence: jwt.sign({ id }, process.env.JWT_SECRET, { expiresIn: '30d' })
recommendation: Pin algorithm explicitly: jwt.sign(payload, secret, { algorithm: 'HS256', expiresIn: ... }) and on verify pass { algorithms: ['HS256'] } to defend against alg=none / alg-confusion. Add a startup check that JWT_SECRET is set and length >= 32 chars.

issue: Stack traces returned to client in any non-production environment; relies solely on NODE_ENV being literally 'production'
evidence: stack: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? null : err.stack
recommendation: Default to safe (hide stack) and only expose when NODE_ENV === 'development'. A misconfigured staging env without NODE_ENV set will leak stack traces, file paths, and library versions.

issue: Token verification errors logged with console.error including full JWT error — can leak token internals into shared logs
evidence: } catch (error) { console.error(error) ...
recommendation: Log only the error name/message (e.g., 'jwt expired') not the full error object, and never log the raw token. Add structured logging that redacts Authorization headers.

issue: User-controlled query.keyword passed straight to MongoDB $regex with case-insensitive flag — ReDoS / NoSQL DoS
evidence: const keyword = req.query.keyword ? { name: { $regex: req.query.keyword, $options: 'i' } } : {}
recommendation: Escape regex metacharacters like in suggestProducts (line 202 already does this). A query of '(a+)+$' or deeply-nested patterns can pin CPU. Also cap keyword length (e.g., 100 chars).

issue: Order totals (itemsPrice, taxPrice, shippingPrice, totalPrice) are trusted from the client
evidence: const { itemsPrice, taxPrice, shippingPrice, totalPrice, ... } = req.body; const order = new Order({ ..., itemsPrice, ..., totalPrice })
recommendation: Recalculate prices server-side from product IDs and qty (fetch Product, multiply price * qty). Currently a user can submit totalPrice=0 and the order is persisted with the attacker's number.

issue: addOrderItems performs no schema validation on orderItems, shippingAddress, paymentMethod — type-confusion / mass-assignment risk
evidence: const order = new Order({ orderItems, ..., shippingAddress, paymentMethod, ... })
recommendation: Add Joi/Zod/express-validator schema for the request body. Without it a client can submit nested objects with operators or unexpected fields.

issue: Multer filename uses raw file.originalname without sanitization — path traversal & arbitrary extension
evidence: cb(null, `review-${Date.now()}-${file.originalname}`)
recommendation: Strip path separators and use a UUID or sanitize via path.basename + allowlist extension. originalname like '../../etc/x' is normalized by multer-diskStorage but extensions like 'image.png.php' still land on disk; also length is unbounded.

issue: fileFilter trusts client-supplied MIME type only — no magic-byte check and no file-size limit (DoS)
evidence: if (file.mimetype.startsWith('image/')) { cb(null, true) } ... multer({ storage, fileFilter }).array('images', 3)
recommendation: Add { limits: { fileSize: 2 * 1024 * 1024 } }. Validate file content with file-type/magic bytes after upload. Restrict to specific MIME (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp).

issue: Server-side fetch to URL built from env var with no allowlist; if N8N_WEBHOOK_URL is ever sourced from untrusted input it becomes SSRF. Also request body is forwarded unbounded.
evidence: const target = `${base.replace(/\/+$/, '')}/feature-control`; await fetch(target, { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(req.body || {}) ... })
recommendation: Validate at startup that N8N_WEBHOOK_URL is https + matches an allowlisted host. Add express.json({ limit: '32kb' }) for this route specifically, validate body shape with Zod before forwarding, and require authentication (this route currently appears mounted without protect — any unauthenticated visitor can drive the n8n webhook through your server using your API key).

issue: POST /api/autopilot/feature-control has no auth middleware — anyone on the internet can use the server as a free proxy to your n8n webhook (also covers your N8N_API_KEY)
evidence: router.post('/feature-control', asyncHandler(async (req, res) => { ... fetch(target, { headers: { ...(apiKey ? { 'X-API-Key': apiKey } : {}) } })
recommendation: Add protect + admin middleware. The whole point of the proxy is to keep N8N_API_KEY out of the browser, but if the route is anonymous, anyone can replay arbitrary feature-control payloads through your authenticated tunnel.

issue: Atomic-write claim is racy and unsafe across concurrent admins: read → mutate → tmp write → rename has a TOCTOU window; concurrent PATCHes can clobber each other
evidence: const data = await readFlags(res); ... data[key].status = status; ... await writeFile(tmp, ...); await rename(tmp, filePath)
recommendation: Serialise writes (in-process mutex, e.g., async-mutex) or move to a proper datastore. The MCP server (mcp-features/index.js writeFeatures) writes the same file from a separate process — there is no cross-process locking, so two admins or one admin + an AI agent can lose updates.

issue: PATCH /:key permits arbitrary `key` from path that becomes a JSON property name — Object.prototype is reachable via __proto__/constructor only on assignment, but data[key] still allows probing existence of inherited keys
evidence: const { key } = req.params; ... if (!data[key]) { ... } ... data[key].status = status
recommendation: Validate `key` against an allowlist regex (e.g., /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$/) before any access, and refuse names like __proto__, constructor, prototype. Otherwise `PATCH /api/featureflags/__proto__` causes confusing behaviour and may expose Object.prototype properties (e.g., toString) via the truthy check.

issue: set_feature_state / adjust_traffic_rollout accept any feature_id string and use it as a JSON property accessor; same prototype-key concern as REST route, plus no validation that feature_id matches expected pattern
evidence: const feature = features[feature_id]; ... feature.status = state; ... writeFeatures(features)
recommendation: Add z.string().regex(/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$/) to the Zod schema for feature_id. MCP tools are reached via untrusted LLM input — treat their args as user input.

issue: HTTP MCP transport defaults to running without authentication when MCP_BEARER_TOKEN is empty — and the empty string is even documented as 'auth disabled'
evidence: const token = process.env.MCP_BEARER_TOKEN || ''; ... app.use('/mcp', (req, res, next) => { if (!token) return next(); ... })
recommendation: Fail-closed: if MCP_TRANSPORT=http and no token (or token shorter than 32 chars) is set, refuse to start. Currently a misdeploy without the env var exposes write tools (set_feature_state) to anyone who reaches port 7777 via the Cloudflare tunnel.

issue: Bearer-token comparison uses === — vulnerable to timing attacks
evidence: if (req.headers.authorization === `Bearer ${token}`) return next()
recommendation: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(received), Buffer.from(expected)) after length check. With remote attackers across the Cloudflare tunnel, even small timing leaks can help.

issue: No audit log for security-relevant events (login, password change, admin update, role change, feature-flag change)
evidence: no logger imports across controllers/middleware
recommendation: Add structured audit log (winston/pino) for: login success/failure, password change, isAdmin change, feature flag mutation. Without this, post-incident triage is impossible.

issue: registerUser accepts any password — no length, complexity, or breach-check requirement
evidence: const user = await User.create({ name, email, password }) — no validation before create
recommendation: Validate email format and password (>= 12 chars, not in HIBP top-list, optionally zxcvbn score) before User.create. Without this, '1' is an acceptable password.

issue: Upload route POST /api/upload has no auth middleware — anyone can upload arbitrary jpg/png to the server filesystem
evidence: router.post('/', upload.single('image'), (req, res) => { res.send(`/${req.file.path}`) })
recommendation: Add protect + admin (only admins create products). Also enforce file size limits via multer { limits: { fileSize } } and validate with magic bytes. Currently unauthenticated users can fill the disk.

issue: admin middleware returns 401 Unauthorized for an authorization failure — should be 403 Forbidden, and the inconsistency obscures monitoring
evidence: if (req.user && req.user.isAdmin) { next() } else { res.status(401); throw new Error('Not authorized as an admin') }
recommendation: Return 403 when authenticated but lacks role; 401 only when missing/invalid token. Easier to alert on brute-force vs privilege-escalation attempts.

file: backend/* (note only, no audit run per scope)
issue: Dependency hygiene not in scope to run, but several backend deps are noted as old in CLAUDE.md (CRA 3.4.3, webpack-dev-server 3.x); express-async-handler is unmaintained
evidence: react-scripts 3.4.3 referenced in CLAUDE.md; express-async-handler last published years ago
recommendation: Run `npm audit --omit=dev` against root and mcp-features/mcp-rag; replace express-async-handler with Express 5 native async handling or asyncify.
